rows.what_is_actually_there: By Ashlyn Cenicola and Robert Mann, Published: August 20, 2026, https://www.financialresearch.gov/the-ofr-blog/2026/08/20/central-clearing-treasury-repos-plateaued/. Three-sentence summary: (1) OFR finds the share of all Treasury repo centrally cleared peaked at ~53% (and 72% for the in-scope non-affiliate, fixed-term subset) around end-2025, then fell and stabilised at ~46% (62% in-scope) through April 2026, and attributes the Q1 2026 decline mainly to G-SIBs, whose cleared share spiked to 55% in December 2025 and fell back to 45% — consistent with year-end G-SIB-surcharge balance-sheet management (surcharge measured at year-end; clearing reduces it via netting/lower risk weights), while non-G-SIBs rose steadily from 40% to 55%. (2) It also says market participants 'may still prefer non-centrally cleared repos', money funds clear <50% (FICC's new Collateral-in-Lieu may help), and hedge-fund reverse repo clears far less than hedge-fund repo because of CCP margining practices (negative haircuts) and pre-netted relative-value packages (68% of HF reverse repo netted per OFR Brief 23-01). (3) Data: OFR's cleared repo and NCCBR collections plus Federal Reserve Bank of New York and Bank of New York Mellon (triparty) data, daily from July 1, 2025 to April 23, 2026 (holidays removed), i.e. shares of repo outstanding, not FICC sponsored CSV.
rows.notes: The blog measures cleared share of all Treasury repo (G-SIB driven), not a fall in the FICC sponsored CSV; the section's 'structural explanation' (dealer balance-sheet/spread incentives after SEC Feb 2025 extension; substitution to NCCBR/triparty) omits OFR's named driver — year-end G-SIB surcharge management.
